questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: My first reason for going on Erasmus was for academic reasons. I wanted to develop my academic profile. However, that was not the only reason I went. I had an expectation of making new relations and experiencing a new culture.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Prague was the best city to study in. The culture, the prices and the people. There is many students living in Prague and many opportunities for Erasmus students everywhere.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I found it quite confusing. The process with pre approval of courses took a long time and I ended up being a little stressed about deadlines. But I will encourage everyone to do it anyway, cause it all ended up working even though there was some bumps on the way.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The Erasmus team from the Faculty of Arts where efficient and very sweet. They sent out emails quite often just to make sure that everybody got the information.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: They had a welcome meeting where all the informations where presented that was very useful.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was not easy. But I joined a lot of Facebook groups and then suddenly there was a room free. You should be very aware of scammers, they are everywhere. My accommodation was offered because other students where searching for another roommate. That too was a little sketchy, but trust the proces and don't transfer any money before you have a contract or a good feeling about it. This was the website that my roommates found the apartment. I lived in Balbinova. You live in a building full of Eramus Student without living in dorm rooms. It is not luxury, but it's okay. I would do it again.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Because I lived with 40 Erasmus student in one building it was never lonely, so I almost felt like there was more a community than they had in the dorm rooms. The dorms of Charles University are not in the city center. So if you want to get the full city experience I would choose to live off campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The good thing about the dorms is that it is easy accessible and a lot cheaper than living off campus.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: When I look back at it now it was quite easy, but while I was doing it I didn't feel like that. I felt it was so confusing and I was a little scared that any minor mistake would do that I couldn't go. But it didn't.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: When I applied for Charles University, I did on an online platform with the regular information. When you where done you where asked to download a PDF and fill it. This was you official application that you needed to get signed both from your home and host university.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: It was easy, and they Erasmus team were a good help if you had any questions. They were a little busy, but I always managed to get through to them when I called by phone.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Some of the courses I applied for from home where not available, so I had to pick new ones. In the first week of the stay everybody have to pick their courses in an online database. So even though your courses where managed befor coming you still had to choose them again.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The database was open for one week and you had to be really quick. If you didn't get a spot, then you could join a waiting list. I did that with 3 courses and got accepted.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There was a lot of courses on Faculty of Arts and you could also choose from other Faculties

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level on the courses where fair. They were not as challenging as the one at my home university. But I think it would be hard for an Erasmus student to follow a harder academic level, because everything is so overwhelming.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I had some excursion courses and that was amazing. But otherwise was the style of teaching very similar with lectures and sometimes group work.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend them all.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Every accommodation you will see will ask for a deposit that is at least 2 months of rent.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Everything is cheaper. But food and cultural offers are the cheapest. Clothing and other materials are a little cheaper

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Didn't really look for them

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Have no idea

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Didn't attend any

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would recommend them to go to the countries around Czech republic. Transport is not expensive. So go to Budapest, Vienna, Bratislava or Dresden. For the other Czech Cities I would recommend Brno and Plzen(but only to see the brewery)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The language was very different. Most czech people spoke English but you will see someone that is not. The Police is a lot harder. They have like a zero tolerance and are happy to give out tickets. You will see a lot of police officers in the streets.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to the Erasmus events. There is a lot of Facebook pages, WhatsApp groups etc. There you will meet hundreds of students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: They will ask you for tips everywhere.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The effectiveness of the everthing in Prague. Everything works perfectly.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Check your email
Be optimistic 
Enjoy

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I got so many new relations that I am very thankful for. And to start fresh in a new city and live there for more a long time was really enjoyable.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: It was so overwhelming in the beginning. Everthing was new, but be patience. After one months it is good again.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Do it! I would recommend Prague to everybody.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
